title: W3 DRAFT: ratios for the state.json normative structures (gates, limits, cost policy, guard)
description: Wave 3 codifies the structures that bind agents without ever having been written as prose rules: human_gates.require_human_approval_for (four items), limits (six bounds), cost_policy.frontier_budget plus its seven numbered rules - five of which exist ONLY in state.json and in no contract document at all - and protected_paths. This wave forces the hardest drafting question in the epic, and the frozen ledger, not you, answers it: a configured constant is not a decision with reasoning attached, so 'max_steps_per_task = 50' is a FACT, not a ratio (the D1 distinction - not every recorded decision binds, and not every configured constant is a decision at all). Codify the NORM the structure enforces; the numbers appear inside the ratio as the values in force. You publish nothing.
acceptance_criteria: OWNS EXACTLY docs/precedent-research/codification-wave3-ratios.md (NEW) plus its ratio text files. MUST NOT write .harness/state.json under any circumstance - this wave READS the file and codifies what it finds. Proposing a change to a limit, a gate item or a cost rule is out of scope and belongs to the section 5A loop plus the human gate.

INPUT IS THE FROZEN LEDGER's wave-3 rows exactly as frozen; a row added, dropped or re-tiered is a DEVIATION: note naming the row, the reason and the new N3. Read T-384's and T-385's verdicts first and state which wave-2 defect each row avoids.

GRANULARITY IS THE LEDGER'S, NOT YOURS: one record per NORM as the ledger fixed it; a record per bare numeric constant is a defect. The four human_gates items are ONE norm (the gate list) unless the ledger says otherwise, and the record must quote all four verbatim without dropping or rewording one.

CITE state.json BY KEY PATH, NEVER BY LINE NUMBER: limits.max_steps_per_task, human_gates.require_human_approval_for, cost_policy.rules[3], protected_paths. The file has grown across four generations and every line-anchored citation into it in this repo has already gone stale (ORCHESTRATION.md:80's state.json:352/356/358 anchors are the worked example). A path:lines token in sources resolves on FILE EXISTENCE ONLY, so a stale range never dangles and never gets caught mechanically.

Their ratios are therefore drafted from the state.json text itself - say so in each record's dicta rather than implying a contract home that does not exist - and anchor tier_evidence to P-030's accepted_mutations entry where it genuinely applies and to nothing fabricated where it does not (CD6).
